desc: South Korean metal products company with copper and processing interests; details limited and not well known to this analyst.
markets: Sells products mainly in Korea. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Commodity metal producer selling to industrial buyers at home; consumer brand building through F1 would add little and cost would be hard to justify.

desc: Malaysian maker of copper rods, wires and cables for electrical and industrial customers, listed on Bursa Malaysia.
markets: Sells copper products in Malaysia and exports to Asian markets. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Commodity metal producer selling to industrial buyers at home; consumer brand building through F1 would add little and cost would be hard to justify.

desc: Abu Dhabi conglomerate investing across healthcare, real estate, finance, technology, food and energy through many subsidiaries.
markets: Subsidiaries operate across the Gulf and in Africa, Asia and Europe; expands through acquisitions and holdings.
rationale: Gulf conglomerate in finance and technology; Abu Dhabi Grand Prix hospitality could serve partners, and sponsorship fits regional ambitions.

desc: Japanese general trading house with businesses in natural gas, metals, mobility, food, industrial materials and retail, including Lawson convenience stores.
markets: Operates in around 90 countries with energy, metals and food interests, and invests in mobility and energy transition projects.
rationale: Global corporate brand with business-to-business customers; F1 hospitality could support partnerships and showcase mobility and energy projects.

desc: Japanese general trading house with textiles, machinery, metals, energy, food and ICT, and owner of FamilyMart and Ito-Chu Fashion.
markets: Operates across Asia, North America and Europe with a large stake in CITIC and growing food and retail operations.
rationale: Consumer-facing brands like FamilyMart and textiles offer marketing angles; hospitality could aid partner networks, but trading houses spend sparingly.

desc: Japanese general trading house with interests in energy, metals, machinery, chemicals, food, mobility and healthcare around the world.
markets: Operates globally, with large LNG and mining assets and investments in mobility and energy transition.
rationale: B2B-focused trading house with a corporate brand; F1 hospitality could aid partner networks but the benefit is difficult to quantify.

desc: Vietnamese conglomerate in real estate, retail and healthcare, and owner of VinFast, with Vinhomes, Vincom and VinFast businesses.
markets: VinFast sells EVs in Vietnam, the US, Europe and Asia and is building a plant in India and North Carolina.
rationale: VinFast could use F1 to build global EV brand awareness in the US and Europe, with Vinhomes hospitality as an extra.

desc: Japanese general trading house with businesses in food, power, infrastructure, metals, chemicals and agriculture, including Gavilon grain.
markets: Operates worldwide, with power projects, grains and metals, and a growing renewable energy portfolio.
rationale: Trading house with industrial customers and limited consumer brand; hospitality for partners is the only clear use.

desc: Hong Kong conglomerate with property (Taikoo Place), Cathay Pacific stake, beverage bottling for Coca-Cola and marine services.
markets: Operates in Hong Kong, mainland China, Southeast Asia and the US, with property, aviation, beverages and marine units.
rationale: Cathay Pacific, Coca-Cola bottling and Taikoo property give hospitality and brand angles, but group has not shown F1 interest.

desc: Japanese general trading house with businesses in metals, transport, infrastructure, media, lifestyle, real estate and mineral resources.
markets: Operates globally, with investments in Jupiter media, retail, mobility and mining projects such as Quebrada Blanca.
rationale: Corporate partner for global customers with some consumer brands such as Summit stores; hospitality is the main use.

desc: Chinese state-owned conglomerate in financial services, advanced manufacturing, resources and energy, including CITIC Bank and CITIC Pacific Special Steel.
markets: Operates in China with assets in Australia, Brazil and the Middle East, including iron ore and special steel.
rationale: State-owned group with banks and manufacturing; F1 offers corporate hospitality, but international brand building is not an evident priority.

desc: Asian conglomerate with stakes in Jardine Pacific, Hongkong Land, Dairy Farm, Mandarin Oriental, Astra and Jardine Cycle & Carriage.
markets: Operates in Hong Kong, mainland China, Southeast Asia and Indonesia, with automotive, retail, property and hotels interests.
rationale: Mandarin Oriental, Astra automotive and Hongkong Land give luxury and automotive angles for Asian Grand Prix hospitality.

desc: Japanese trading house in the Toyota Group dealing in automotive, metals, chemicals, energy and Africa-focused businesses.
markets: Operates worldwide with large automotive distribution in Africa and Asia, and invests in energy and mobility.
rationale: Toyota-group trading arm with African and Asian car distribution; Toyota Gazoo Racing link could support B2B hospitality and brand.
f1: Toyota Group member (Toyota Gazoo Racing - Haas F1 team title partner)

desc: Indian conglomerate arm of the Adani Group investing in airports, mining, data centres, roads and new energy businesses.
markets: Operates in India with mining in Australia, plus airport and infrastructure incubation; expanding into data centres and green hydrogen.
rationale: Group seeking global visibility; the Indian market and airport passenger brand could benefit, but governance scrutiny raises reputational risk.

desc: South Korean Samsung Group arm in construction, trading, fashion and resorts, with a major stake in Samsung Electronics.
markets: Operates globally in construction, trading and fashion, with infrastructure projects in the Middle East and Asia.
rationale: Construction and trading arm of Samsung with fashion and resort brands; hospitality could support B2B clients in the Gulf.

desc: Hong Kong conglomerate with ports, retail (A.S. Watson), infrastructure, telecoms (Three) and energy businesses across Europe and Asia.
markets: Operates in more than 50 countries, with ports, Watsons retail, telecoms in Europe, and infrastructure.
rationale: Watsons and Three consumer brands give marketing angles in Europe and Asia, and port business hospitality, though group is conservative.

desc: South African group that mainly holds a large stake in Prosus and owns South African media and fintech assets.
markets: Holds Prosus stake with investments in Tencent, e-commerce and fintech across Europe, India, Brazil and elsewhere.
rationale: Investment group with e-commerce brands; brand-building through F1 is more relevant for its operating companies than the holding.

rationale: Infrastructure owner with little consumer branding; F1 hospitality offers some B2B value, but a limited partnership structure makes sponsorship unlikely.
